title: Descent of the closed exceptional coefficient mate to the etale site
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and $1\le m\le n$. Set $A=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi^n)$, $B=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi^m)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. For a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $Y$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], write $a_Y:Y\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $F_{Y,R}=Ra_{Y,R!}\dashv G_{Y,R}=a_{Y,R}^{\times}$, $\omega_{Y,R}=G_{Y,R}R_s$, and $\varepsilon_{Y,R}:F_{Y,R}\omega_{Y,R}\to R_s$, for $R=A,B$, on ordinary small etale module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-amb-etale-compact-support, thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. Let $T_Y=-\otimes_A^LB$ [def-kun-derived-tensor], and denote the canonical compact-support coefficient comparison by $c_{Y,K}:T_sF_{Y,A}K\to F_{Y,B}T_YK$ [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change]. Here bounded constructible finite-Tor means constructible cohomology, zero outside a finite interval, and integers $a\le b$ such that tensoring with every degree-zero module sheaf has cohomology only in $[a,b]$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes, def-kun-tor-amplitude]. Let $i:Y\hookrightarrow P=\mathbf A^r_k$ be a closed immersion with $Y$ affine. Set $M=\omega_{P,A}$, $N=I_AM$, $M_B=T_PM$, where $I_R=Ri^!_{\mathrm{et},R}$ and $e_{R,H}:i^{\mathrm{et}}_{R*}I_RH\to H$ is its counit [lem-exc-closed-ambient]. For $W=Y,P$, write $S_{W,R}=\nu_W^*$, $U_{W,R}=R\nu_{W,*}$ for etale/pro-etale comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], and $T_W^{\mathrm{pro}}=-\otimes_A^LB$ on the pro-etale site. Use its specified unit $\eta_{R,H}:H\cong U_{P,R}S_{P,R}H$, the $B$-linear tensor comparison $t_{W,K}:S_{W,B}T_WK\cong T_W^{\mathrm{pro}}S_{W,A}K$, the transported closed functor $J_R=S_{Y,R}I_RU_{P,R}$, and $\alpha_{R,H}=S_{Y,R}I_R(\eta_{R,H}):S_{Y,R}I_RH\cong J_RS_{P,R}H$. Let $\delta_{R,L}:S_{P,R}i^{\mathrm{et}}_{R*}L\cong Ri^{\mathrm{pro}}_{R*}S_{Y,R}L$ be the canonical counit-mate direct-image comparison. These are the comparisons of [lem-coef-site-closed-counit-transport, lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Then the map $b^e_{i,M}:T_YI_AM\to I_BM_B$ uniquely defined by
$$e_{B,M_B}\circ i^{\mathrm{et}}_{B*}(b^e_{i,M})=(T_Pe_{A,M})\circ(c^e_{i,N})^{-1}$$
is an isomorphism; here $c^e_{i,N}:T_Pi^{\mathrm{et}}_{A*}N\cong i^{\mathrm{et}}_{B*}T_YN$ is the ordinary direct-image coefficient comparison [lem-coef-finite-direct-image]. More precisely its site image is $\kappa_2^{-1}b^{\mathrm{pro}}\kappa_1$, where $\kappa_1=T_Y^{\mathrm{pro}}(\alpha_{A,M})t_{Y,N}$, $\kappa_2=J_B(t_{P,M})\alpha_{B,M_B}$, and $b^{\mathrm{pro}}$ is the counit-defined finite pro-etale closed-shriek comparison at $S_{P,A}M$ [lem-coef-finite-closed-shriek, def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. In this formula $J_R=S_{Y,R}I_RR\nu_{P,R,*}$. Write $c^p_{i,Q}:T_P^{\mathrm{pro}}Ri^{\mathrm{pro}}_{A*}Q\to Ri^{\mathrm{pro}}_{B*}T_Y^{\mathrm{pro}}Q$ for the canonical pro-etale direct-image coefficient map [lem-coef-finite-direct-image]. The ordinary and pro-etale coefficient maps satisfy the normalized square
$$c^p_{i,S_{Y,A}N}\circ T_P^{\mathrm{pro}}(\delta_{A,N})\circ t_{P,i_*N}=Ri^{\mathrm{pro}}_{B*}(t_{Y,N})\circ\delta_{B,T_YN}\circ S_{P,B}(c^e_{i,N}).$$
The coefficient components at both $S_{Y,A}N$ and $J_AS_{P,A}M$ are invertible. The descent uses full faithfulness only on $T_YN,I_BM_B$ and faithfulness only on $\operatorname{Hom}(i_{B*}T_YN,M_B)$, all bounded-below independently of $b^e_{i,M}$. No preservation of all $D^+$ by $T$ and no unbounded pro-etale exceptional adjoint is asserted. For empty $Y$ the comparison is the unique isomorphism in the zero derived category.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3: application of finite closed-shriek coefficient change to the Tate input; descent from its pro-etale statement with the actual coefficient and counit maps; extraction of the expanded retained stage-1 proof, steps 13,14,15,16

proof.text: Establish all domains before constructing the comparison. By [lem-coef-dualizing-closed-site], $M,N,M_B,I_BM_B$ and their indicated site images are bounded constructible finite-Tor, and the maps $t,\alpha,\delta$ have the specified normalizations. Choose a finite Tor interval $[a,b]$ for $N$. The etale version of [lem-sf-flat-model] represents $N$ by a flat complex $Q$ zero outside $[a,b]$. Consequently $T_YN$ is represented by $Q\otimes_A B$, also zero outside $[a,b]$, so it is bounded below, without assuming $T$ preserves all $D^+$. By [lem-coef-dualizing-closed-chart], $i_*^{\mathrm{et}}$ is exact termwise and commutes with cohomology. Thus $i_{B*}^{\mathrm{et}}T_YN$ is bounded below as well. In particular both endpoints of $\operatorname{Hom}(i_{B*}^{\mathrm{et}}T_YN,M_B)$ and both objects $T_YN,I_BM_B$ lie in their ordinary etale $D^+$ independently of the desired comparison.

source.place: Paragraph 3: domain audit for application of closed-shriek coefficient change and descent

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-etale-proetale-scalar-mate] with $f=i$ and $J=N$. The map $i$ is finite, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated, by [lem-coef-dualizing-closed-chart]; step 1 verifies both boundedness hypotheses. Its $\beta^R$ is precisely our $\delta_R$: both are the canonical counit-mate comparison with the normalization in [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. Its tensor comparison $\delta_{W,-}$ is $t_{W,-}^{-1}$, the canonical comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Its $\gamma$ is our $c^e$ or $c^p$, because [lem-coef-finite-direct-image] defines these by that same coefficient-adjunction transpose. Substitution in its displayed equality gives
$$i_{B*}^{\mathrm{pro}}(t_{Y,N}^{-1})c^p_{i,S_{Y,A}N}=\delta_{B,T_YN}S_{P,B}(c^e_{i,N})t_{P,i_{A*}N}^{-1}T_P^{\mathrm{pro}}(\delta_{A,N}^{-1}).$$
Postcompose with $i_{B*}^{\mathrm{pro}}(t_{Y,N})$ and precompose with $T_P^{\mathrm{pro}}(\delta_{A,N})t_{P,i_{A*}N}$ to obtain exactly the normalized square in the statement. This is an equality of actual $B$-linear morphisms.

source.place: Paragraph 3: normalize the ordinary/pro-etale direct-image coefficient square

proof.text:
The quotient $B$ is finite as an $A$-module (it is cyclic). Apply [lem-coef-finite-direct-image] to $i$ and the bounded constructible finite-Tor etale input $N$ of step 1. This gives invertibility of $c^e_{i,N}$ and of $c^p_{i,S_{Y,A}N}$. Put $H=S_{P,A}M$, $Q=S_{Y,A}N$, $K=J_AH$, and $a=\alpha_{A,M}:Q\xrightarrow{\sim}K$. Naturality of the pro-etale coefficient comparison gives
$$c^p_{i,K}\,T_P^{\mathrm{pro}}(i_{A*}^{\mathrm{pro}}a)=i_{B*}^{\mathrm{pro}}(T_Y^{\mathrm{pro}}a)\,c^p_{i,Q}.$$
The other three maps in this equality are isomorphisms. Solving for $c^p_{i,K}$ proves its invertibility, so both coefficient components specified in the item are invertible. This also fixes the component used by the exceptional comparison; it is not an arbitrary identification of the direct images.

source.place: Paragraph 3: invertibility at both site-origin and transported-exceptional inputs

proof.text:
The input $H=S_{P,A}M$ is bounded constructible finite-Tor by [lem-coef-dualizing-closed-site]. Apply [lem-coef-finite-closed-shriek] to the quotient $A\to B$ and $i$. Its finite exceptional functor is the specified transported $J$ on these inputs. It supplies an isomorphism
$$b^{\mathrm{pro}}:T_Y^{\mathrm{pro}}K\longrightarrow J_BT_P^{\mathrm{pro}}H,$$
with counit identity
$$E_{B,T_P^{\mathrm{pro}}H}\,i_{B*}^{\mathrm{pro}}(b^{\mathrm{pro}})=T_P^{\mathrm{pro}}(E_{A,H})(c^p_{i,K})^{-1}.$$
All terms are in the permitted bounded-below etale-origin domain. Indeed the source is isomorphic to $S_{Y,B}T_YN$ through $\kappa_1=T_Y^{\mathrm{pro}}(a)t_{Y,N}$; the target is isomorphic to $S_{Y,B}I_BM_B$ through $\kappa_2=J_B(t_{P,M})\alpha_{B,M_B}$. These are isomorphisms because $t,\alpha$ are and functors preserve inverses. Thus no unbounded pro-etale exceptional adjunction is needed.

source.place: Paragraph 3: apply the finite pro-etale closed-shriek comparison to the Tate input

proof.text: Set $f=\kappa_2^{-1}b^{\mathrm{pro}}\kappa_1:S_{Y,B}T_YN\xrightarrow{\sim}S_{Y,B}I_BM_B$. By [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] and the independent bounds in step 1, full faithfulness gives unique morphisms $b:T_YN\to I_BM_B$ and $d:I_BM_B\to T_YN$ mapping to $f$ and $f^{-1}$. Since $S_{Y,B}(db)=1$ and $S_{Y,B}(bd)=1$, faithfulness on these bounded-below Hom sets gives $db=1$ and $bd=1$. Hence $b$ is an isomorphism and has exactly the site image asserted in the statement. It remains to identify $b$ with the named counit-defined ordinary comparison.

source.place: Paragraph 3: descend the conjugated isomorphism using only the bounded-below Hom sets

proof.text:
For the remaining calculation abbreviate $i_{R*}^{\mathrm{pro}}$ to $q_R$, $T_W^{\mathrm{pro}}$ to $T_W^p$, $S_{W,R}$ to $S_{W,R}$, and set $v=t_{P,M}$, $w=t_{Y,N}$, $\delta=\delta_{A,N}$, $\delta'=\delta_{B,T_YN}$, $c_Q=c^p_{i,Q}$, $c_K=c^p_{i,K}$. The counit naturality equation at $v:S_{P,B}M_B\to T_P^pH$ is
$$E_{B,S_{P,B}M_B}\,q_B(J_Bv)^{-1}=v^{-1}E_{B,T_P^pH}.$$
The normalized exceptional-counit transport [lem-coef-site-closed-counit-transport] gives
$$E_{A,H}\,q_A(a)\,\delta=S_{P,A}(e_{A,M}),\qquad E_{B,S_{P,B}M_B}\,q_B(\alpha_{B,M_B})\,\delta_{B,I_BM_B}=S_{P,B}(e_{B,M_B}).$$
Its hypotheses $M,N,M_B,I_BM_B\in D^+$ hold by step 1. Naturality of $\delta_B$ at $b$ and $\kappa_2 f=b^{\mathrm{pro}}\kappa_1$ therefore give
$$S_{P,B}(e_{B,M_B}i_{B*}^{\mathrm{et}}b)=v^{-1}T_P^p(E_{A,H})c_K^{-1}q_B(T_Y^pa)q_B(w)\delta'.$$
Here we used the pro-etale counit identity of step 4; each composition has source $S_{P,B}i_{B*}^{\mathrm{et}}T_YN$ and target $S_{P,B}M_B$.

source.place: Paragraph 3: explicit exceptional-counit conjugation, first half

proof.text:
Use the naturality equality from step 3 in the inverted form $c_K^{-1}q_B(T_Y^pa)=T_P^p(q_Aa)c_Q^{-1}$. Substituting it into step 6 and then using its $A$-counit transport identity gives
$$S_{P,B}(e_Bi_*b)=v^{-1}T_P^p(S_{P,A}e_A)T_P^p(\delta^{-1})c_Q^{-1}q_B(w)\delta'.$$
The normalized square of step 2, with invertible components as proved in step 3, is equivalent to
$$T_P^p(\delta^{-1})c_Q^{-1}q_B(w)\delta'=t_{P,i_{A*}N}S_{P,B}(c^e_{i,N})^{-1}.$$
Finally naturality of $t_P$ at $e_A:i_{A*}N\to M$ says $v^{-1}T_P^p(S_{P,A}e_A)t_{P,i_{A*}N}=S_{P,B}(T_Pe_A)$. Consequently
$$S_{P,B}(e_Bi_*b)=S_{P,B}((T_Pe_A)(c^e_{i,N})^{-1}).$$
These are substitutions, cancellation of inverse isomorphisms and naturality; no additional geometric comparison or hidden interchange lemma is used.

source.place: Paragraph 3: explicit exceptional-counit conjugation, cancellation of the normalized coefficient square

proof.text:
By step 1 both maps compared in step 7 belong to $\operatorname{Hom}(i_{B*}^{\mathrm{et}}T_YN,M_B)$ with bounded-below endpoints. Faithfulness of $S_{P,B}$ from [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] therefore gives
$$e_{B,M_B}\,i_{B*}^{\mathrm{et}}b=(T_Pe_{A,M})(c^e_{i,N})^{-1}.$$
The ordinary adjunction $i_{B*}^{\mathrm{et}}\dashv I_B$ of [lem-exc-closed-ambient] makes the assignment $h\mapsto e_{B,M_B}i_{B*}^{\mathrm{et}}h$ a bijection from $\operatorname{Hom}(T_YN,I_BM_B)$ to $\operatorname{Hom}(i_{B*}^{\mathrm{et}}T_YN,M_B)$. Thus the displayed equality characterizes $b$ uniquely as $b^e_{i,M}$. Step 5 proves it is an isomorphism and identifies its site image. Only the full-faithfulness Hom sets in step 5 and this bounded-below ambient Hom set were used.

source.place: Paragraph 3: faithfulness descends the actual counit equation, then ordinary adjunct uniqueness

proof.text: If $Y$ is empty, the only sheaf of modules on its small site is zero, so its derived category has one object and one morphism. All $Y$-objects and $Y$-maps above are zero; the comparison and its inverse are the unique morphism. The normalized square has zero source and target and its equalities still hold. If $m=n$ the scalar functors and their coefficient maps are identity comparisons, so the same counit uniqueness gives the identity exceptional comparison. The argument does not use $r>0$, so also includes $r=0$.

proof_origin.place: Paragraph 3: expanded bounded-below descent using existing normalized scalar and counit comparison lemmas; categorical cancellation follows Stacks Tag 0B65, categories.tex, lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints.
